title: Advice From A Stubborn Irish Dad: Tried And Tested By A Stubborn Irish Daughter
description: A Memoir of Love, Lessons, and the Unshakeable Wisdom of an Irish Dad When you lose a father young, the sudden silence in the house is deafening. But as the initial shock of loss begins to settle, you realize something extraordinary: his voice hasn’t gone quiet at all. It’s still echoing off the kitchen tiles, popping up every time you attempt to check the oil in the car, navigate a crisis, or decide whether a coat is really necessary for a two-minute walk to the shop. Written just one month after the sudden passing of her father, this deeply moving, hilarious, and soul-affirming memoir is an only child’s tribute to a man who was quietly ahead of his time in every way that truly mattered. Born in the 1970s, he was a hardworking lad who poured pints, walked miles home under freezing Irish skies, became a father at twenty-two, navigated separation with grace, went back to college in his forties to master IT, and bought ice cream for every kid on the road. He possessed no formal degrees in psychology or nutrition, yet his practical, kitchen-table logic solved life’s greatest anxieties, one cup of Lyons tea and a slice of buttered toast at a time. Through every stage of life, his unconventional directives served as a lifeline: On Mental Health: Timing panic attacks on a ten-minute wall clock decades before exposure therapy had a name, and declaring "You can’t take on the world" when university burnout hit. On Boundaries & Self-Worth: Advising "If he wants to bring you to dinner, but you don't want to go to dinner, say no!" and proclaiming "I'm a vicious animal!" when his daughter wanted a guard dog. title: Work Like a Pro: Planning, Estimating and Communication Habits for Software Testers, Devel
description: Tired of promising two hours and taking four? In any office, tech, or fast-paced team environment, technical skill alone isn’t enough. You can write clean code, catch critical bugs, or build complex reports, but if your estimates constantly slip, your updates are vague, and you're constantly fighting fires, your reputation takes the hit. Written by a QA Automation Engineer with over four years of real-world experience, Work Like a Pro is a practical, no-nonsense system for mastering the "work around the work." It bridges the gap between technical ability and professional dependability. Inside, you will learn how to: Plan Before You Run: Use a simple five-minute pre-flight checklist to stop diving headfirst into rework. Estimate Honestly: Overcome the planning fallacy, break tasks down, and use three-point estimation to give timelines you can actually keep. Communicate with Trust: Master a four-part standup update formula and stop letting bad news become a late-day surprise. Time-Box Your Day: Defeat distraction, manage constant interruptions, and stop trying to finish everything at once. Be Visible: Make your quiet contributions seen without awkward self-promotion. Packed with real-world examples from software testing and development, these habits apply universally to project coordinators, business analysts, support teams, graduates, and office professionals juggling multiple priorities. Stop burning out and start working smarter. Includes a complete appendix of ready-to-use templates, scripts, and a 14-day starter plan.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_0"]', '#CardInstancedXXUgRs36HJpkUQw639BFA')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_0',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_a

title: Are You Sure You Want to Work in a Restaurant?: The Truth Nobody Tells You, Written by a C
description: Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year's Eve. You'll be at work. On TV, restaurant life looks like a dream: celebrity chefs, perfect plates, spotless kitchens. The reality is different: shifts that end at one in the morning, weekends and holidays sacrificed, kids you only see asleep, stress, exhaustion and an ordinary paycheck for a life that is anything but ordinary. In this book, a working cook tells you, with no filter, everything nobody tells you before you step into a kitchen, onto a dining room floor or behind a bar. Inside you'll find: the truth about hours, holidays, family, pay, your body and stress the good side of the job, the part that keeps you going what happens when, at 30 or 40, you want out but it's too late a 50-question test with three possible results space for your reflections and advice to build a plan B For every role: cook, pizza maker, pastry cook, dishwasher, server, bartender, front desk. title: Road to Work, Book 1: The Learner’s Road: Beginner’s Edition, Part 1 of 2: How We Learn, t
description: Every office is a highway, and your first day is your first lesson. Book 1 of the Road to Work series is a warm, funny, and practical field guide for people at the start of the road: students, interns, new hires, and career changers. Follow Jo Merritt from a nervous first morning at Northbound & Co. through her first real stretch of road, and learn how to drive with confidence, kindness, and a smile. What you will find inside Side-by-side Field Guide cards. Every character is shown twice, as the driver on the road and the person at the office, with a call sign, a memory hook, and one "try this" tip. Two lessons in every chapter. A kind way to grow past a habit, and real encouragement for the good driver next to it. Nobody here is the villain. How we learn. Mentors for every vehicle, learning by watching, reading, and doing, and asking for help without apology. Helpers and motivators. The instructor, the crossing guard, the honest mechanic, the pit crew, and the people who make every road safer. Habits that last. Fuel, rest, and service intervals for a whole career, plus a Monday Morning Checklist and thirty days on the road. Road to Work, Book 1: The Learner’s Road is Part 1 of 2. When you are ready for detours, conflict, heavy loads, and leadership, continue with Book 2, The Long Haul . Both books are also available together in the Complete Edition . Climb in. Buckle up.
